html:
SMTO-SKL-0060 — SMTO couldn't find a Microsoft 365 account it can use

GUID: 2dfca651-fa98-5839-8f77-dd9e13712fad
Slug: microsoft365-account-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO looked for a connected Microsoft 365 account to do this, but the one named doesn't exist, or none of your accounts is signed in with permission for this kind of action. Nothing was done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO "show my connected Microsoft 365 accounts" and check whether the account you want is listed and signed in. SMTO can only use Microsoft accounts that have been connected and are still signed in.
  2. If it's missing or needs signing in again, ask SMTO to "connect my Microsoft account for calendar changes" (or whatever you need) and approve Microsoft's sign-in page. Each kind of action, such as reading mail or changing the calendar, needs its own permission when you connect.
  3. If SMTO says no Microsoft app is set up, ask the person who manages SMTO to add a Microsoft OAuth App in Parameter Store first. SMTO needs that one-time Microsoft app setup before any account can be connected.
  4. When asking again, type @ and pick the connected account so SMTO uses exactly that one. Naming the account stops SMTO from searching for a suitable one by itself.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists the account as connected and completes your request using it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details, which list the permissions needed, and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Microsoft 365 administrator.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The named Microsoft 365 account does not exist in Parameter Store, or no connected account has the permissions and active sign-in this operation needs.

What this means

  • Exact account lookup is absent or no eligible Microsoft account can satisfy selection. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Exact account lookup is absent or no eligible Microsoft account can satisfy selection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect exact account_ref and required-feature eligibility.

How to fix it

  • Check Parameter Store for a microsoft365_account record: if the explicit account_ref is absent, correct it; if records exist, compare their authorized_features and authorization_state with the required_features in the error details. Connect or reconnect the account with microsoft365.connect (auth_app_ref of a configured Microsoft OAuth App) requesting the missing features, then select it explicitly.
  • Create/connect a Microsoft 365 Account in Parameter Store or provide an exact eligible account_ref.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account is connected and explicitly selected.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
